newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-STICH KNOCKED OUT OF AUSTRALIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-STICH KNOCKED OUT OF AUSTRALIAN OPEN.

text.p: German 15th seed Michael Stich followed compatriot Boris Becker out of the Australian Open on Wednesday, beaten in five tough sets by Ukrainian Andrei Medvedev in the second round.

The former Wimbledon champion took an early lead in the match under the centre court floodlights but Medvedev, a 24-year-old ranked 36 in the world, powered back to take the next two sets before winning 4-6 6-1 6-2 4-6 9-7 in three hours and 27 minutes.
Becker, the sixth seed and defending champion, was bounced out by Spaniard Carlos Moya in five sets in the operning round on Monday.
Bathed in sweat, Medvedev used a blistering backhand and superior court speed to upset Stich, whose usually booming serve misfired and who committed unforced errors at crucial times.
Stich, cursing and throwing his racquet in frustration, staged a fightback to win the fourth set and keep his chances alive, but blew an opportunity to break Medvedev early in the deciding set.
Though urged on by the crowd, the German failed to find his rythm and finally handed Medvedev the match with another unforced error -- a backhand into the net.
Medvedev next meets Dutchman Dennis van Scheppingen for a place in the final 16.
